title: Intake-to-claim mapping of policy, insured vehicle and property; POST /claims answers handling
story: Claims created through claimant and CSR intake carry policy number, insured vehicle/property so coverage verifies and glass claims fast-track for Aurelia.
acceptance: mapping.js exports async enrichClaimCreate(input,{session,answers,questions,getSnapshot}) returning ClaimCreate with policyNumber (answer mapped to policyNumber, else session.policyNumber), vehicles[] containing role insured with vin/unit matched from the policy snapshot, and a properties[] insured_location entry for property LOBs; toClaimCreate stays synchronous and backward compatible
Selection by VIN (case-insensitive) or unit id; when no match or no snapshot the input is returned unchanged (no throw) and the result reports unmatched
node --test tests/unit/intake/mapping-enrich.test.js passes (VIN match, unit match, no match, missing policy number, property LOB)

node --test tests/unit/intake/glass-fasttrack.test.js passes: unit test submits a glass claim through intake service, and a createApp integration test for tenant aurelia shows the created claim has coverage verified (not needs_review) and fast-track routing/flag

POST /claims either persists answers per ClaimCreate contract or returns 400 for unknown properties; chosen behavior follows the contract, is documented in the result, and is covered by node --test tests/unit/claims/create-answers.test.mjs
No files outside listed paths changed; existing intake and claims tests still pass
brief: Gap: intake submit calls toClaimCreate (src/modules/intake/mapping.js) which never sets the insured vehicle, and policyNumber only if a question maps to it. Coverage then cannot match and stays needs_review, blocking STP. Build: (1) in mapping.js add exported async enrichClaimCreate(input,{session,answers,questions,getSnapshot}). Policy number: first an answer whose question mapsTo policyNumber (already handled in toClaimCreate), else session.policyNumber (session start). Then call getSnapshot(policyNumber) (injected; real impl is mod('coverage').getPolicySnapshot via ctx; check its exact signature in architecture/core-runtime-api.md and modules.md coverage section). Find the selected vehicle: a vehicle-type answer or an answer carrying vin/unit; match case-insensitive on VIN, or on unit id, against snapshot.vehicles; copy vin, year/make/model and unit onto the insured vehicle entry (role insured). For property LOBs map the loss location/insured property into properties[role=insured_location] using the snapshot property if one exists. Never throw on lookup failure: log and return input unchanged. Do not store PII in logs. (2) Wiring: ic-workflow-security-hardening (ticket S4-WFL-02) owns service.js and will call mapping.enrichClaimCreate if it exists via namespace import; you must not edit service.js. Therefore your glass-fasttrack integration test must run after both tickets merge; also unit-test enrichClaimCreate directly with a small local fake snapshot in mapping-enrich.test.js so you are not blocked. Use tests/unit/intake/fakes.mjs and helpers.mjs, read only. (3) POST /claims in src/modules/claims/routes.mjs silently drops `answers`. Check ClaimCreate in the openapi/Claim schema: if answers is a defined property persist it (encrypted if x-pii), else reject unknown properties with 400 and the standard error envelope. Post the decision to the workflow hub. Pitfalls: Aurelia glass fast-track depends on a policy with glass coverage in tenants/ seeds; use only synthetic seed data; do not hardcode tenant ids.

verdicts.reason: All criteria met; 98 intake/claims unit tests pass, e2e+security 368 pass 0 fail; intake-to-claim idempotency test failure is S4-WFL-02's, flagged to its owner
